steps.what: Furring at 406 mm over WRB; corner boards.
Window trim kits per opening, belly band, then siding.

benefits.value: 7.9 h saved on 237 trim pieces (about CAD 365)
benefits.detail: Assumes 3.0 min per trim piece measured and cut on site versus 1.0 min with a labelled, pre-cut part, at CAD 46.2/h loaded. Replace with your own time study.

benefits.value: 9.1% cut waste vs 10% typical order allowance
benefits.detail: Acucut 1D nester on this trade's 237 sticks: 115 boards, 612.65 m stock for 556.98 m of parts (bundle-window constrained runs add about 0.5 points). Conventional allowance 5 to 15% (BuildingScience). Difference about 6 bf, CAD 4 at CAD 700/MBF (estimate).

FMI puts rework at about 5% of construction spend and 48% of rework on poor communication or data. If labelled, sequenced, pre-checked parts prevent 15 to 30% of this trade's rework (estimate), callbacks fall by 0.75 to 1.50% of trade spend.

cell_does: Cuts furring at 406 mm per wall, corner boards, belly band with mitred outside corners.
Cuts 13 picture-frame trim kits with 45 degree mitres from the model's unit sizes.
cell_cannot: Cut fibre-cement or vinyl siding (dust and blade type); trim and furring only.

addons.name: Fibre-cement blade + dust extraction
addons.why: Cut lap siding to length per course

app: Scan a trim piece: window and position.
code: BCBC 9.27 (cladding), 9.27.2.2 capillary break / rainscreen (required in most of BC coastal climate)
summary: Rainscreen furring, corner boards, belly band and picture-frame window trim cut with 45 degree mitres from the window sizes in the model.
highlight: 13 mitred window and door trim kits plus rainscreen furring for 129 m2 of wall, labelled by opening.
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
